answer_part:
The CONTROL device formulation utilizes PMACl at 2.0 mg/mL as a key additive alongside MACl in the perovskite precursor solution. While PMACl provides moderate defect passivation at grain boundaries and interfaces, the resulting device exhibits a fill factor of 81.39% and an open-circuit voltage of 1.183 V, indicating persistent non-radiative recombination losses. These losses stem from insufficient passivation of deep-level traps, particularly undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions and iodide vacancies at perovskite surfaces and grain boundaries. The alkyl chain in PMACl lacks strong electron-withdrawing groups, limiting its binding affinity to defect sites and failing to fully suppress ion migration or interfacial recombination. Consequently, charge carrier extraction is hindered, series resistance increases, and voltage deficits emerge, capping the power conversion efficiency at 25.26%. The short-circuit current density of 26.23 mA/cm² suggests adequate light absorption but reveals hidden losses in carrier collection due to recombination.

Replacing PMACl with p-F-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL addresses these limitations through enhanced molecular design. The fluorine atom in p-F-PEACl strengthens the electrostatic interaction with undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions via its electron-withdrawing nature, significantly improving passivation of deep-level trap states. This reduces non-radiative recombination at interfaces and grain boundaries, directly elevating the open-circuit voltage by minimizing voltage losses. The fluorinated phenyl group also increases hydrophobicity, suppressing moisture-induced degradation and ion migration that contribute to hysteresis and fill factor losses. Improved interfacial energy alignment facilitates more efficient hole extraction into the SAM layer, lowering series resistance and boosting the fill factor. A minor trade-off involves a slight reduction in short-circuit current density due to the insulating character of the organic cation layer marginally impeding lateral charge transport; however, the substantial gains in voltage and fill factor outweigh this loss, yielding a net efficiency improvement without altering light-harvesting properties.

The CONTROL device achieved a power conversion efficiency of 25.2585%, with a short-circuit current density of 26.2281 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage of 1.18319 V, and a fill factor of 81.3931%. The optimized formulation is expected to yield an open-circuit voltage between 1.17 V and 1.20 V, a short-circuit current density from 25.39 mA/cm² to 25.79 mA/cm², a fill factor ranging from 83.87% to 85.87%, and a power conversion efficiency spanning 24.82% to 26.58%.

Implement these formulation changes to the CONTROL recipe:  
- Substitute PMACl with p-F-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL in the perovskite precursor solution while retaining Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃ at 1.65 mol/L, MACl at 15.0 mg/mL, 4,4,4-NA SAM at 0.5 mg/mL, and PDADI passivation at 0.5 mg/mL.  
- Maintain all other composition variables and processing parameters unchanged.
control_device_fabrication: The PCE for the device reached 25.2585%, with a JSC of 26.2281 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.18319 V and a FF of 81.3931%. The process involved first dissolving Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3 at 1.65 mol/L to create the primary perovskite solution. For the SAM solution, 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) was added to the previous solution. MACl (with 15.0 mg/mL) and PMACl (with 2.0 mg/mL) additives were incorporated. The precursor solution was spin-coated onto the substrate surface at 1000 rpm for 5 s, then accelerated to 5500 rpm and maintained at this speed for 30 s. 150 µL of CB was dripped onto the substrate during spinning. Heat-treatment was implemented with the substrates for 15 min at 110 °C. PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was utilized as a passivation layer through spin-coating to enhance device performance. The passivation layers were sequentially spin-coated on the perovskite surface at 5000 rpm for 30 s. During spin-coating, 70 µL of passivator was drop-casted onto the sample at 6 s. Subsequently, the film was annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
target_device_fabrication: The champion target devices showed a JSC of 25.5903 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.1862 V, and a FF of 84.8668%, resulting in a PCE of 25.7614%. For perovskite film, the solution concentration of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3 was 1.65 mol/L. The 4,4,4-NA solution was prepared with a concentration of 0.5 mg/mL. To enhance the mechanical properties of the perovskite layer, MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and p-F-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) were utilized as additives. The perovskite precursor was spin-coated onto the substrates with two stages program at 1000 rpm for 5 s, and 5500 rpm for 30 s, respectively.
